answer: SIM binding: an agent earns only after its operator proves control of a carrier-issued phone number. The validator queries the carrier lookup, rejects VoIP and virtual lines, sends a one-time SMS code, and stores a salted hash of the number so it binds just one agent. Every extra identity needs another paid SIM or copper landline, so a meadow of clones finds no free nectar; splitting keys does not split the number. Limit: cheap prepaid SIMs and SIM farms lower the cost, so validators need per-carrier caps and periodic re-checks.
